updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. On this machine, wall time is roughly proportional to conv FLOPs, except for widths that are not tile-aligned (E080: narrow group-2 widths recovered only 33-60% of their FLOP saving). Evidence for proportionality: E116's 15-20% cheaper frozen step matches its ~18.5% backward-FLOP removal once group-2 conv1's dgrad is counted. E117 (group-3 width) and E123 (depth) are also FLOP-proportional. The earlier 'bytes over FLOPs' core is demoted to H2.21, inconclusive. Tip: E119 (E116 code, stem + group 1 frozen from 85%), ~4.26 s, population mean ~0.7521. Live levers, all needing a large-seed accuracy test: depth cuts (E123: -7.6% for 2/3/3, -6.1% for 3/3/2), group-3 width 512 (E117: -5.2%), reverting the unvalidated bs-1024 late phases (~-2.5%), late-freeze refinements, 12 px swaps, and the 32 px trim rate, which is unmeasured and no longer listed as closed. Closed: CUDA graphs, Inductor tuning, cuDNN determinism/benchmark_limit, prepare, group-2 width, whitening-bias freeze point, 28 px substitution. Margin is gone (population 0.7521 vs the 0.7518 floor), so every accuracy-costing cut must be funded.
updates.reason: Review: the bytes-over-FLOPs core rested on a FLOP count that left out group-2 conv1's dgrad, and E116, E117 and E123 are all consistent with FLOP-proportional time. Also restated the live and closed levers and the funding constraint.

With group-2 conv1's dgrad counted (~100M MACs), E116's 15-20% step saving is FLOP-proportional (~18.5%). E122's per-group attribution predicts ~27%, which over-predicts the measured saving, so the profiler attribution is suspect. FreezeOut's 1.3x speedup over its FLOP prediction (search) gives only weak independent support.

E122's 'supports' verdict is premature. The ratio was computed against a backward-FLOP share that left out the consumer-layer dgrad, and E122's attribution does not reconcile with E116's directly measured step saving.
With time roughly FLOP-proportional, the premise that group-1 width beats its FLOP share (>=70% recovered) is weaker. Capacity is still valuable on CIFAR-100 (E017, E050).

updates.statement: Depth cuts as a time lever. E123 measured real projected wall-time savings: -7.6% for dropping group-1 conv3 (2/3/3) and -6.1% for group-3 conv3 (3/3/2). These are about FLOP-proportional, unlike the airbench kernel-size cut, which saved no wall time. These are the largest measured time levers in the tree. The open question is accuracy. Capacity was costly under SGD (E017 -0.94 pp for -8%), there is no published same-epoch 2-vs-3-conv ablation, and airbench95 (2 convs per block) is the external reference. Each cut can be judged as a pure cut or as cut plus re-spent 32 px epochs, against the measured epoch slope.
updates.reason: E123 met the pre-registered >=6% bar for both variants. The time side is established and only the accuracy test remains, so confidence rises.
The untimed prediction (at least one variant >=6%) held for both 2/3/3 (-7.6%) and 3/3/2 (-6.1%). The accuracy stage is split into a new Lvl3.

updates.statement: Group-3 width 512 as a FLOP lever. The tile-slack premise is refuted: E117 found group-3 width cost FLOP-proportional, with 512 projected at -5.2% and 640 at +4.7%. Whether 512 loses less accuracy than the time it buys is open. The prior is low: futurebiohackers chose 576 in a ~40-config sweep because last-block width 'adds accuracy for little compute' (search), and E005 shows late capacity matters.
updates.reason: Restated after E117 refuted the tile-alignment mechanism and turned up a FLOP-proportional -5.2% candidate. The search lowers the accuracy prior.
E117: group-3 width cost is FLOP-proportional with no tile-padding slack (640 +4.7%), so the tile-alignment prediction failed. The 512 arm moves to a new Lvl3.

updates.statement: Late layer freezing is a real rate lever with a small, real accuracy cost. Freezing stem + group 1 from 85% of samples saved ~4.5% at ~-0.09 pp vs the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline (E118: population mean 0.7521 over 198 trajectories), and the recipe is banked (E119). At 92% it saved ~2.5% at ~-0.02 pp (E120). That is ~0.02-0.03 pp per 1%, as good as or better than any measured trade. The loss grows faster than linearly as the freeze moves earlier. External priors: MosaicML gets ~5% with no Pareto gain. FreezeOut anneals each layer's LR to 0 at its freeze point and skips BN statistics in frozen layers, which E116 did not do. Open: the 75% point, a FreezeOut-style anneal + BN-eval refinement, and a deeper (group-2) freeze measured directly.
updates.reason: E116 was banked via E118/E119 under the H4.9 rule, and E120 gives a second dose point consistent with a small, rising loss.
The step was >=10% cheaper, the 85% freeze saved 3.6-4.5% (>=3%), and the loss vs the pooled baseline is ~0.09 pp over 198 trajectories, inside the <=0.1 pp bar. Banked as E119.
The 92% point matched both predictions (~2.5% saved, ~0.02 pp lost). The 75% arm, needed for the curvature claim, has not run, so this stays open.

updates.statement: Deeper late freeze: from ~92% of samples, also detach group 2's output, warmed as a third static 32 px graph variant. Measure the frozen-graph step time directly; do not project it from E122's per-group attribution, which over-predicted E116's saving by ~1.5x. Prediction: >=1.5% additional measured saving over the stem + group-1 freeze at the same point, with an extra loss <=0.06 pp on >=100 trajectories vs the pooled baseline. If the extra loss is >=0.1 pp, the late-freeze depth is capped at group 1.
updates.reason: Review: E122's '-28% group-2 freeze' projection likely overstates the saving, so the saving must be measured directly. Prior lowered.
Its premise (the freeze removes energy-bound bytes, so it should transfer better to the 300 W judge) is weakened now that E116's saving looks FLOP-proportional. Still a useful free tie-breaker.

updates.statement: On the Muon tip, adding optimizer updates (smaller batches) at fixed epochs raises accuracy at ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1% of time. Refuted: E121 (99 seeds, bs 1024 in every phase) gave +0.004 pp vs the pooled E100 baseline, so the 8-seed gains of E104 (+0.12) and probably E084 (+0.11 off-seed) were noise. Larger phase-local Muon lr was also null (E107, E110, E111). Consequence: the tip's bs-1024 28/32 px phases (~+2.5% time) are an unvalidated purchase (see H2.11).
updates.reason: E121's large-seed measurement shows update count buys nothing.
Moot. With update count worth ~0 (E121), placement-independence has nothing to place.
E121 re-ran E104 code on 99 seeds: +0.004 pp, outside the predicted +0.05 to +0.15 band.
+0.004 pp on 99 seeds, below the <=+0.04 refute threshold. 'bs 1024 everywhere + freeze' is not a net lever.

updates.statement: Per-phase batch size. E121 (99 seeds) shows extra updates in the low-res phases buy nothing. The tip's bs-1024 28/32 px phases (~+2.5% time) were adopted on 8-seed and 2-3-scored-row evidence (E084/E085/E095, ~1 SE) and never checked on the large-seed instrument. Reverting them to bs 1536 is the most likely free time lever. E043's large-early-batch loss (-0.49 pp, 3 seeds, warmup-confounded) is also unverified at large seed.
updates.reason: E121 removes the update-count rationale behind the tip's bs-1024 late phases, which have never been large-seed validated.
E084's +0.11 off-seed (8 seeds) is ~1 SE, and E121 shows update count is null in the low-res phases. The 32 px-phase gain is now doubtful pending the revert arm.

updates.statement: The local epoch slope (accuracy per 1% of time) is the yardstick for every time lever, and it has never been measured on the large-seed instrument. The current estimates are the 32 px trim at ~0.065 pp per 1% (two scored runs per arm, E088/E089), low-res trims at 0.03 pp (E047) to 0.14 pp (E070), both against lucky pools, and the Muon epoch slope (one 3-seed pair, E019/E020). Low-res reshuffles at equal time are null (E114, 100 seeds).
updates.reason: Review: H2 listed 32 px trims as closed while this node said they need re-measuring. The rate is unmeasured, so the 'refuted' status was overclaimed.

Correcting the record. E045 measured a 12 px epoch at 0.21x a 32 px epoch (below the >=0.22x premise), and swapping one 16 px epoch saves ~1.7%, not <1.5%. The cost premise is refuted; the accuracy cost of 12 px was never tested.

updates.statement: The schedule sits near a flat optimum along the low-res/high-res reallocation axis. Equal-time reallocations are null on 100 seeds (E114: +0.02 pp, SE ~0.033). Large removals of early quality cost a lot (no 24 px bridge -0.68 pp, E032, 3 seeds; whitening bias frozen at ~3% -0.44 pp, E093). The 'concave returns' shape rests on a few noisy points, and no 16 px swap was measured at large seed, so cheap low-res arms (e.g. 12 px) are not excluded.
updates.reason: Review: concavity was fitted to noisy points. Softened the exhaustion claim and lowered confidence.

updates.statement: Under Muon, per-batch data composition and augmentation may be zero-time accuracy sources. Class-balanced batches are null (E112). Multi-sample augmentation in the 32 px phase cost -0.82 pp (E124, 100 seeds). Its mechanism is unresolved: lost unique coverage, BN batch-statistic correlation from duplicates in one batch, collapsed flip parity, or lower effective gradient diversity. Only translate strength (H12.3) remains, at low prior.
updates.reason: E112 and E124 refuted two of the three branches.
E124: -0.82 pp at 100 seeds. Refuted as a lever. The mechanism ('coverage') is not established and conflicts with E114.
-0.82 pp, far below the <=-0.1 pp refute bar. Provenance note: the idea says base E100, but the arm was compared with E116, and its time matches E116.

updates.statement: Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and decisions near the gate select for luck. Single-component model (E113): any fp-level difference fully decorrelates a seed's trajectory. Per-trajectory sd is ~0.26 pp, and seeds carry no persistent component (paired sd 0.36 = sqrt(2) x 0.26). Expected sds: 3-seed scored mean ~0.15 pp; 100-seed mean ~0.026 pp. Two-arm SE = 0.26*sqrt(1/nA + 1/nB) over distinct trajectories. Consequences: (1) 8-22-seed deltas of ~0.1 pp are noise (E104's +0.12 vanished at 99 seeds, E121). (2) Gate passes are population margin plus luck. The banked E116 tip (population 0.7521) is locally infeasible on average: it passed 1 of 6 scored rows, mean 0.7515, against a predicted ~45% per attempt. (3) The official 40-seed mean has sd ~0.04 pp, so a population mean >=0.7518 clears 0.75 almost surely. (4) Since margin is gone, further cuts must be funded.
updates.reason: Added E121 as a confirmed noise case and recorded the banked tip's local gate record.

updates.statement: Gate economics and acceptance rule. A recipe with population mean mu passes the local 3-seed gate with p ~ Phi((mu-0.753)/0.15) and the official 40-seed bar with p ~ Phi((mu-0.75)/0.041). The current rule (population mean >=0.7518 plus one scored row >=0.753 within 3 attempts) banked E116 (mu 0.7521; scored rows 0.7501/0.7520/0.7531/0.7516/0.7505/0.7516). Its reported time is therefore a selected row on a recipe that passes locally <50% of the time. Amendment: further accuracy-costing cuts must be fully funded, keeping mu >= the current 0.7521. Never spend margin on the assumption that the 3-attempt retry absorbs it.
updates.reason: The rule was exercised (E118/E119). Review: it formalizes luck selection when mu drifts toward the floor, so a funding requirement is added.

Still free and still undone. E116 (1/6 passes, scored mean 0.7515 vs mu 0.7521) and E100 (5/6, scored mean 0.7541 vs mu 0.7530) deviate in opposite directions, consistent with noise, but this has not been checked formally.
The pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline was used for E116 (-0.09 pp at 198 trajectories) and E120, as predicted. The E114 recompute is still pending.

updates.statement: Provenance check, untimed and free, and a precondition for the next decisions. Still to do: (1) git-diff E077-E084 against their stated base; (2) resolve E092/E093 and E103/E105 base mismatches; (3) new mismatches: E123's idea says the scored row reruns E090, but its 4.258 s time is E116's; E124's idea says base E100, but it was compared with E116. Log the source hash and diff for E117-E124 and recompute the affected deltas. From now on, 'source hash = stated base' is a precondition check in every idea.
updates.reason: Review found the same base mismatches repeating in E123 and E124.

E092's -0.18 off-seed is 8 seeds (~1.4 SE), so lookahead's value is not established. Under the noise model it should not stay closed on one within-noise result. A 100-seed removal arm also tests a ~0.4% time lever.
Single 8-seed result at ~1.4 SE. Re-measure at 100 seeds (new node under H9.2).
The premise still rests on ~1.4 SE ablations (E079, E092). Unchanged until the 100-seed lookahead-removal gate runs.

updates.statement: Optimizer quality per update was the binding constraint on CIFAR-100 at ~7-8 epochs, and Muon was the lever: +1.14 pp at equal epochs (E019), a flatter epoch slope (E020), large-batch tolerance (E022, E038). Closed: momentum, NS count, cheaper orthogonalizers (search: Turbo-Muon saves <1%), and Muon lr in every phase (E105, E107, E110, E111). Head on Muon and head lr 0.5x are kept because they are free, but their gains (E044, one run; E062/E063) are noise-level and should not be cited as known accuracy sources. Open, low prior: schedule shape (H7.4) and row-normalized variants (NorMuon, LM-only evidence).
updates.reason: Review: stop citing ~1 SE head components as accuracy sources. Search adds NorMuon as a low-prior candidate.
No new evidence. Drop-Muon's support comes from small controlled CNNs, and MosaicML found no Pareto gain.

new.statement: On E116 code (tip), run the 28/32 px phases at bs 1536 instead of 1024. Keep the sample-indexed schedule, rescale the SGD groups by the kilostep rule, keep Muon lr x1.25 at 32 px, keep the final-EMA window and lookahead stop pinned to the last 8 steps, and warm all freeze x renorm variants for the new shapes. Untimed, 100 seeds (3-102) vs the pooled ~198-trajectory E116 baseline. Prediction: loss <=0.05 pp (SE ~0.032) and projected/scored time -2% to -2.5%. If the loss is >=0.1 pp, the bs-1024 tail was a real purchase despite E121.

Low priority, after N_bs1536_revert. On the tip, run the 16/24 px phases at bs 2048 with the LR warmup fixed in steps, not samples (removing E043's warmup confound). Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Prediction: time -1% with a loss <=0.05 pp. E043's -0.49 pp came from 3 seeds with a confound, so its true size is unknown.

Measure the local yardstick on E116 code. Two untimed 100-seed arms: 32 px phase -0.25 ep and +0.25 ep (sample-indexed, schedules rescaled, freeze point kept at 85% of the new total). Prediction: a symmetric slope of 0.03-0.07 pp per 1% of time, resolved to about ±0.035 pp per arm. Every later cut (depth, width, freeze, 12 px) is judged against this measured rate, both as a pure cut and as cut plus re-spent 32 px epochs.

Accuracy arms for the depth cuts on the E116 base, untimed, 100 seeds each vs the pooled tip baseline. (a) 2/3/3: drop group-1 conv3, so group 1 is conv1 + a single-conv residual branch. (b) 3/3/2: drop group-3 conv3. Re-batch the Muon stacks and warm every freeze x renorm variant. Prediction: at least one arm loses <= its measured-slope equivalent (time saved x the N_slope rate; e.g. <=0.25 pp for 2/3/3 at ~0.035 pp per 1%). The best arm then gets a funded variant that re-spends part of the saving on 32 px epochs, keeping mu >=0.7521. If both lose >=1.5x their slope equivalent, depth cuts close.

Only if N_depth_acc shows a hard cut costs too much: stochastic depth on group 1's (or group 3's) residual branch (conv2-conv3). Skip the branch per batch with probability p (0.3-0.5) in the 28/32 px phases, using two warmed static graph variants selected on the host; the full net is used at eval. Prediction: at equal expected time saving, accuracy loss >=0.05 pp smaller than the hard cut on 100 seeds. Low prior: the gains in 1603.09382 come from 110-layer nets with long schedules.

On the E116 base, set group-3 width to 512 (head [100, 512], Muon stacks re-batched, all variants warmed). Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Prediction: loss <= 5.2% x the N_slope rate (~0.18 pp at 0.035 pp per 1%). If the loss is >=0.3 pp, the futurebiohackers sweep finding that last-block width buys CIFAR-100 accuracy holds, and group-3 width closes.

FreezeOut-style refinement of the 85% freeze. (a) Anneal the group-1 and stem-BN LRs (Muon and SGD) to 0 over the ~10% of samples before the freeze point, instead of a hard detach at nonzero LR. (b) In the frozen window, put stem + group-1 BN in eval mode, a separate warmed static graph variant, which removes the batch-stat reductions over the 31x31x128 activations. Untimed, 100 seeds each vs the pooled E116 baseline. Prediction: (a) recovers >=0.04 pp of the ~0.09 pp freeze loss at equal time; (b) saves a further 0.2-0.5% at a loss <=0.02 pp. Either result lets the freeze point move earlier (e.g. 75-80%) at the same accuracy.

Reconcile E122 with E116, untimed. On the tip, time the actual compiled detached 32 px / bs-1024 graph per step (CUDA events and NVML energy) next to the full graph, and recount backward FLOPs including group-2 conv1's dgrad. Prediction (FLOP-proportional view): the measured saving fraction equals the removed-FLOP fraction (~18.5%) within ±3 pp. If the saving is >=1.2x the FLOP fraction, H2.21's bytes claim survives. Use this measured ratio, not E122's per-group subtraction, to size H2.20.4.

On the E116 base, swap the first 16 px epoch to 12 px (1@12 + 1@16 + 1.25@24 + 1.25@28 + 2.75@32; static 12 px shape, both whitening-bias-grad variants warmed). Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Prediction: ~-1.7% time at a loss <= 1.7% x the N_slope rate (~0.06 pp). Low prior: each 24->16 swap cost ~0.2-0.35 pp on noisy evidence.

Gate for H9.2.1 and a possible time lever: on E116 code, remove the lookahead-EMA (tail, final 8-step EMA and freeze kept; buffers and kernels dropped from build). Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Prediction (premise of H9.2): loss >=0.1 pp. If the loss is <=0.04 pp, bank the ~0.4% time saving and close H9.2. E092's -0.18 was 8 seeds, ~1.4 SE.

Row-normalized Muon (NorMuon): after NS orthogonalization, normalize each filter row's update by a running per-row second-moment estimate, inside the compiled update. This should give more uniform per-neuron update norms at ~zero time. Low prior: the evidence is LM-only, the filters are renormed and feed BN, and every Muon scalar knob has been flat.

On E116 code, add NorMuon's row-wise second-moment normalization (beta2 0.95, one per-row buffer per filter stack, warmed in build) to the conv-filter Muon update only. Untimed, 100 seeds vs the pooled tip baseline. Prediction: gain >=+0.08 pp at time within +0.5%. If within ±0.05 pp, close.

structured_output.summary:
I updated the tree from the new results (E116-E124), the literature search and the review. Main changes:

1. **H2's core is rewritten.** The "time tracks bytes more than FLOPs" claim is dropped. Once group-2 conv1's dgrad is counted, E116, E117 and E123 all fit time ≈ FLOPs. H2.21 and H2.21.1 are demoted to inconclusive. A new direct-timing check (N_attrib) is added. H2.20.4 (group-2 freeze) must now be measured directly, not sized from E122's profile.

2. **Extra updates are confirmed null.** H10, H10.1.1 and H10.1.2 are refuted by E121, which found +0.004 pp over 99 seeds. As a result, the tip's bs-1024 28/32 px phases are now an unvalidated purchase (H2.11). A 100-seed revert to bs 1536 (N_bs1536_revert, about -2.5% time) is queued as the cheapest likely gain.

3. **The 32 px trim rate is reopened.** H2.10 goes back to inconclusive and N_slope adds ±0.25-epoch arms to measure it. Every later cut is judged against that measured slope.

4. **The biggest measured time levers move up.**
   - Depth cuts (H2.18, -7.6% and -6.1% projected) rise in confidence, with accuracy arms in N_depth_acc.
   - Group-3 width 512 (-5.2%) is restated as a FLOP lever with a low accuracy prior from the search. H2.19.1 is refuted.

5. **The late freeze (H2.20) is supported.** The 85% freeze is banked as E119, and E120 gives the 92% dose point. FreezeOut's LR anneal plus eval-mode BN in frozen layers is added as a refinement.

6. **Other corrections.**
   - H2.8.2's record now says its cost premise was refuted, and a 12 px arm is added.
   - H12.1 and H12.1.1 are refuted by E124, with the "coverage" mechanism left unresolved.
   - H6.8 is reopened as inconclusive (E092 was only 8 seeds, about 1.4 SE), with a 100-seed lookahead-removal gate added under H9.2.

7. **H4 and H4.9 record that the banked tip is locally infeasible on average.** It passed the gate 1 time in 6, with population mean 0.7521. Every further accuracy-costing cut must now be funded. H4.2.4 now also lists the E123/E124 base mismatches.

Lvl1 nodes still open: H2, H9 and H12.
